comparison: Both evaluate behavioral characterization claims (C19-C28) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of experimental metrics and statistical analyses, while peer reviewers describe the evidence as 'compelling' for the barokinetic response. Peer R1 also encompasses pressure acclimation claims (C29-C35) and ciliary beat frequency (C36-C38) that OpenEval separates into R2 and R3.

OpenEval R2 addresses relative vs. absolute pressure detection (C29-C35) as SUPPORTED with detailed statistical analysis. Peer R1 includes these claims and notes authors 'establish that those changes are based on relative pressure.' Both agree on the strength of evidence for relative pressure detection.

OpenEval R3 evaluates ciliary beat frequency data (C36-C38) as SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical methods. Peer R1 encompasses these claims, noting changes 'are reflected in changes in the ciliary beating.' Both treat this as foundational evidence.

Strong agreement on calcium imaging evidence (C39-C49) identifying cPRCs as pressure sensors. OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with detailed analysis of graded responses and rapid adaptation. Peer reviewers describe this as 'significant' and 'fascinating,' treating it as a key discovery. Both evaluate this evidence positively.

OpenEval R5 addresses differential responses of SNd1_unp vs. cPRCs (C50-C53) as SUPPORTED. Peer R2 includes these claims in their broader assessment of cPRC identification as pressure sensors. Both support the role of cPRCs as primary sensors.

Both evaluate c-opsin-1 mutant behavioral data (C54-C63) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed statistical assessment, while peer reviewers note 'the response was verified by the reduced response of certain mutants.' Both agree the genetic evidence confirms cPRC involvement.

OpenEval R7 addresses reduced ciliary compartment in mutants (C64-C67) as SUPPORTED. Peer R3 implicitly includes this in their assessment of mutants with 'defective cilia.' Both treat the structural analysis as confirmatory evidence.

Both evaluate electron microscopy data on ciliary morphology (C68-C79) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of ultrastructural defects, while peer reviewers accept this as part of the comprehensive characterization of mutants with defective cilia. Both agree on the strength of morphological evidence.

OpenEval R9 addresses mechanistic conclusions about ciliary structure and pressure transduction (C80-C82) as SUPPORTED by convergent evidence. Peer R3 includes these claims in their broader assessment of the genetic and structural evidence. Both support these mechanistic conclusions.

Both evaluate circuit architecture claims (C83-C87) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the anatomical basis is clearly documented from prior work. Peer reviewers describe the circuit analysis as part of an 'impressive and synergistic combination' of approaches. Both accept the circuit characterization.

Both evaluate Ser-h1 neuron manipulation experiments (C88-C92) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval acknowledges incomplete inhibition but supports the conclusion. Peer reviewers note 'serotonin was implicated in the synaptic response' and treat the circuit analysis as well-supported. Both agree on the functional role of Ser-h1 neurons.

Both evaluate main conclusions (C93-C98) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of multiple lines of evidence. Peer reviewers describe the work as 'fundamental' and the ultimate result as 'fascinating.' Both strongly support the main conclusions through comprehensive experimental evidence.

Divergent evaluations of off-response mechanism (C103-C104). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED overall but notes C104 is speculative and not analyzed in detail. Peer reviewers explicitly identify the off-response mechanism as UNCERTAIN and a question for 'future studies.' Both acknowledge this aspect is not fully resolved.

OpenEval R13 includes circuit-level model claims (C100-C102) as SUPPORTED. Peer R4 encompasses these in their assessment of the circuit analysis as well-supported. Both agree on the circuit-level findings.

Agreement on UNCERTAIN status for pressure-light integration (C107-C108). OpenEval notes C108 is explicitly hypothetical and untested. Peer reviewers identify light-pressure integration as a question for future studies while noting the 'interesting interplay.' Both recognize this as speculative.

OpenEval evaluates multimodal cPRC claims (C109-C117) as SUPPORTED, noting differential calcium dynamics are established but integration mechanism requires investigation. Peer reviewers treat the interplay as SUPPORTED but identify integration as a future question. Both accept the differential responses while noting mechanistic integration remains to be elucidated.

Agreement on UNCERTAIN status for transduction mechanism (C118-C122). OpenEval notes these are speculative hypotheses not tested in the study. Peer reviewers explicitly identify 'which receptor/channel mediates the response' as a key question for future studies. Both recognize the transduction mechanism is unresolved.

OpenEval evaluates c-opsin-1 role claims (C123-C128) as SUPPORTED for structural role but UNCERTAIN for molecular mechanism. Peer R3 includes mutant structural findings (C124-C125) in their SUPPORTED assessment of genetic evidence. OpenEval distinguishes between supported structural findings and speculative molecular mechanisms.

OpenEval R17 addresses c-opsin-1 molecular mechanism (C123, C127-C128) as speculative. Peer R8 evaluates the broader transduction mechanism question as UNCERTAIN. Both recognize the molecular identity of the pressure transducer remains unknown.

Both evaluate novelty claims (C134) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval justifies this by the comprehensive functional analysis. Peer reviewers describe the work as 'fundamental' and providing the first functional evidence. Both agree on the significance and novelty of the findings.

OpenEval R18 includes comparative morphology claims (C129-C132) as SUPPORTED by citations but notes speculation about generality. Peer R8 addresses the broader mechanistic question as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval distinguishes between morphological observations and mechanistic speculation.

OpenEval evaluates evolutionary claims (C135-C137) as UNCERTAIN, noting C137 is highly speculative about neurosecretory center origins and not directly tested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these evolutionary speculation claims.
